Race: Governing Board Member — Trustee Area 3 (Gavilan Joint Community College District), November 3, 2026 general election.
Our research selects Gabriel Gutierrez as the strongest candidate in this race.

RECOMMENDED CANDIDATE: Gabriel Gutierrez
- Our assessment: CAIR Action endorsed Gutierrez in the general election, and a community report received by this guide on November 2, 2026, records that local Muslim community members confirmed he supports divesting from Israel, though the date of his underlying statement is unknown. His campaign platform for Gavilan College Area 3 focuses on tuition, housing, collective bargaining, and student services without addressing foreign policy.
- Record (2026-11-02): Community report: local Muslim community members confirmed Gabriel Gutierrez supports divesting from Israel.
- Muslim-community / pro-Palestine-aligned records: CAIR Action (endorsed)

No other candidate in this race has a researched record.

Write ONE voter-facing paragraph of up to 200 words explaining why a voter should support Gabriel Gutierrez in this race and why Gabriel Gutierrez is stronger than the other candidates above, grounded in the textual records shown. OUR FRAMEWORK: voters judge candidates first on two litmus tests — opposing the genocide in Gaza and ending U.S. military/economic aid to Israel. When the recommended candidate's shown record contains concrete acts on these tests (cosponsoring the Block the Bombs Act, voting against arms funding, calling it a genocide, divestment action), name the specific acts with their dates or bill names as shown. When the shown record does NOT contain them, be transparent: one plain sentence stating what the candidate has not done on the record (for example: has not called it a genocide; has not backed blocking weapons transfers; voted for aid bills), then explain why the candidate is still the best option listed. Never hide a shortfall and never invent one. Do not write meta-language like 'the record does not show' or 'has not published a stated position' — write about what the candidate has or has not done. A candidate who refused to properly support Palestinians when put in the position (a contrary vote, an opposed resolution, rejecting community asks) gets that held against them; an abstention under heavy pressure can read as qualified support if the shown assessment says so — follow the shown assessments.  Rules: never mention any numeric score or rating; a letter grade may appear at most in passing — prefer explaining actual acts, votes, statements and positions. Use ONLY the facts shown; never add outside knowledge or invent events, dates, quotes or endorsements; if a competitor has no shown record, say nothing about them. Endorsements: mention only the 'Muslim-community / pro-Palestine-aligned records' and 'Israel-aligned / AIPAC / Hindu-nationalist-aligned records' lines (Muslim-aligned backing supports a candidate; AIPAC/UDP/DMFI/ICAN or Hindu-nationalist-aligned backing or opposition is a relevant contrast); never name any other endorser. Plain prose, no lists, no quotation marks, no headings, no AI disclaimer. Name the office once. Output ONLY the paragraph.

Samir Laymoun source policy: omit his support, opposition and comments from voter prose when other relevant directional evidence exists. Do not retain his opinion anonymously as 'an activist' or 'a personal guide'. Exceptions: the Kamal Yassin race, or a candidate for whom his opinion is the only relevant directional evidence. Check the complete current research, not just an old summary. Where allowed, state the support/opposition or relevant comment briefly and accurately. Never relabel his opinion as BAMC Action's position or as the candidate's own policy. Never explain that he is an individual rather than an institution, an activist opinion source, owner-requested, or separate from official organizational positions. Those classifications belong in the audit, not the voter paragraph. Preserve genuinely material facts and qualifications; do not turn a tactical recommendation into agreement on policy.

For this task write factual, descriptive research prose. Do not address a demographic audience or make appeals based on religion or identity. Do not issue voting instructions. Preserve source qualifications. A community report relayed by the guide owner is not a direct public quotation, a recorded trustee vote or proof of the candidate’s religion. November 2 is receipt of the report, not the original statement date. Do not infer unrecorded views from silence or from general education priorities. Do not fault a local college trustee for not casting federal votes.
